reason: V1 had ten demands but no matching action groups. Its donor bank imposed source-file and constructor restrictions before address analysis.
mechanism: Extract source-owned receiver actions independently of whether that receiver has its own assertion.
Build one source-global bank of closed actions with resolved method write summaries.
Index the bank by declaration owner and written field.
Query the index with each existing observation's read demand BEFORE allocating demand/action pair attempts.
Solve receiver/key substitutions and materialize source edits; oracle applicability remains unassessed.

contrast.control: receiver_only: query the shared full bank by declaration owner
contrast.treatment: address: query the same bank by declaration owner plus observed field, then unify the key
contrast.pair_schedules: May differ because the retrieval constraint is part of the tested algorithm.
contrast.query_truncation: None before global round-robin pair scheduling
contrast.scope: This compares two new modes on the same indexed-demand population; it is not an ablation against the full historical 16/17 generator.

independent_checks: Verify exact lookup membership and schedules, shared source domains, uncapped queries, source provenance, AST novelty and all preprocessing costs. No native influence or oracle validity follows from these checks.
scope_limits: Keep the indexed-read demand fragment unchanged; no plain-field or case-specific expansion.
Existing closed-literal argument transport may still prevent real source writers from entering the bank.
The alias literal provenance correction distinguishes the address key-use span from the actual literal-definition span.
This is a narrow test of a constructive search mechanism; academic novelty and task-level benefit remain unestablished.
